items.title: CIA tracked Khamenei for months before Israel struck Tehran

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Prior to Iran attacks, CIA assessed Khamenei ...

items.description:
The CIA monitored Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's movements for months before identifying a rare gathering of Iran's top political and military leaders at a government compound in central Tehran on Saturday morning, providing the intelligence that enabled Israel to launch a precision strike killing Khamenei and more than 40 senior officials, according to reports from The New York Times citing people familiar with the operation.[1][2]

The agency passed what officials described as "high fidelity" intelligence on Khamenei's location to Israel, prompting U.S. and Israeli forces to accelerate the timing of a joint military campaign that had been weeks in planning. The breakthrough came when CIA sources learned that Khamenei would be present at the compound alongside senior security aides for a Saturday morning meeting, rather than the evening session originally expected.[3][4][5]

items.title: US calls Iran's claim it struck USS Lincoln a 'lie'

featured_image.name: USS Abraham Lincoln strike group nears Iran amid rising tensions

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed on Sunday that it struck the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln with four ballistic missiles in the Persian Gulf, a claim the US military swiftly and forcefully rejected as a "LIE."

The IRGC issued the claim as part of what Tehran calls Operation True Promise 4, a retaliatory campaign following joint US and Israeli strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. If confirmed, the strike would have marked the first direct hit on a US aircraft carrier in decades. But US Central Command left no room for ambiguity.

items.title: Brent crude surges to $80 as Iran conflict shuts Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: How could the U.S. strikes in Iran affect the world's oil supply?

items.description:
Brent crude surged roughly 10 percent to about $80 a barrel in off-market transactions on Sunday, as U.S. and Israeli military strikes on Iran threw global energy markets into turmoil and effectively shut down one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints.[1][2]

The spike came as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — a narrow waterway responsible for more than 20 percent of global oil transit — ground to a halt after Iran's Revolutionary Guards contacted vessels to declare the strait closed. Iranian state television reported that an oil tanker attempting to pass through the strait was struck and was sinking, broadcasting footage of a burning vessel at sea.[3][4][5][6][7]

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared the Strait of Hormuz closed to all maritime traffic on Saturday, broadcasting warnings over naval radio that no ships would be permitted to transit the waterway, according to Reuters. The move came hours after the United States and Israel launched joint military strikes against Iran in what President Donald Trump called "major combat operations," an operation dubbed "Epic Fury".[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran faces leadership vacuum after Khamenei killed in U.S.-Israeli strikes

featured_image.name: A placard calling for regime change in Iran

items.description:
The killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Saturday has plunged the Islamic Republic into its deepest leadership crisis since the 1979 revolution, with no clear successor and competing factions already maneuvering for power.

Iranian state television and the state-run IRNA news agency confirmed the 86-year-old's death early Sunday, following what President Donald Trump described as "major combat operations" launched alongside Israel against Iranian military and government targets. Trump called the moment "the single greatest chance for the Iranian people to take back their Country".[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran forms temporary leadership council after Khamenei killed in US-Israeli strikes

featured_image.name: Trump Says Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei Is Dead

items.description:
Iran has set in motion its constitutional succession process after state television confirmed that Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed during coordinated US-Israeli airstrikes on Saturday, marking the most profound rupture in the Islamic Republic since its founding nearly five decades ago.

A temporary leadership council composed of President Masoud Pezeshkian, judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei, and a jurist member of the Guardian Council — selected by the Expediency Discernment Council — has assumed the duties of the supreme leader, according to Iranian state news agency IRNA. Mohammad Mokhber, one of Khamenei's advisers, confirmed in a televised interview that the transition was being carried out under Article 111 of Iran's constitution, which governs the interim period following a supreme leader's death.[1][2][3]

items.title: Regional toll mounts as Iran and Israel trade strikes through the day

featured_image.name: Iran fires missiles at Israel in retaliation for strikes on ...

items.description:
Iran launched waves of ballistic missiles and drones at Israel and multiple Gulf Arab nations on Saturday, hours after the United States and Israel began a joint military offensive against Iranian targets that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and struck military and nuclear sites across the country.

The Iranian counterattack targeted not only Israel but also US military bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and Jordan, marking one of the broadest regional escalations in decades. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps vowed the strikes would continue "until the enemy is conclusively vanquished".[1]
